To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there is no “arrow of complexity,” and (ii) the three types of progress (local, historical, and universal) are distinct, and that the first two can be detected in a reproducing coevolutionary system.
• Evolutionary progress can be measured and predicted.

(a) there exists no universal “arrow of complexity”; (b) adaptive Darwinian evolution can be detected by measuring the Fitness Transmission of a reproducing population; (c) coevolutionary progress can be classified in three types, which are useful for the understanding of the dynamics of coevolution; (d) coevolution can be implemented in 3D virtual worlds with physically realistic creatures; (e) Evosphere is a new 3D virtual world with physically realistic creatures
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of evolutionary dynamics in artificial systems.
the evolution of complex adaptive behaviour in artificial systems, and with the analysis and understanding of the dynamics of coevolutionary processes.
the analysis of coevolutionary systems, and with the detection and measurement of evolutionary progress in them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
evolution is indeed a powerful and creative process, but that its dynamics are complex, and that it does not exhibit a clear “arrow of progress”.

evolution is a creative process which is able to produce complex, unpredictable dynamics, but that it is also capable of producing progress in the sense of increasing performance, and that it is not a process of increasing complexity.
, in coevolution, there is a clear and consistent notion of performance, and three types of progress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by providing a set of concepts, methods and tools, this thesis contributes to making artificial evolution more predictable, analysable and understandable.
, while we have not yet found a general theory of evolution, we have made some progress in our understanding of its basic mechanisms and dynamics.
we have provided a solid theoretical foundation for coevolutionary research.
The main takeaway from our work is that

coevolutionary processes can be understood and analysed in terms of the concepts of performance and evolutionary progress, and that the latter are best understood in the light of the distinction between local, historical, global, and other forms of progress.
, by carefully distinguishing between different types of progress and by using suitable statistical methods, we can detect and analyse the dynamics of evolutionary experiments.
, contrary to popular belief, adaptive evolution can be reliably detected in coevolving populations, and that the concepts of progress and complexity are well-defined and can be studied in detail.
